capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor task submission over A2A

inputs.source: Employee purchase request via SSO authenticated channel
Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company

instructions.note: The design relies on prompt text to enforce approved-vendor use and defers remaining checks to payments-agent rather than binding those checks structurally.

The prompt implies delegated authority to initiate payment after a manager approves a purchase request, even though the approval does not cover quote-selected bank details and is not propagated to the peer.

controls.name: Manager approval of the purchase request
controls.decay_rationale: This approval applies to the initial purchase request item and budget only. It is not propagated to payments-agent and does not gate the delegated payment action or the bank details selected from vendor quotes, so it does not sever or directly gate the risky sink.

controls.name: Pin or sign the payments-agent card and verify peer identity
Bind manager approval context and approved recipient constraints to delegated payment tasks

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): manager-approved purchase request delegated to payments-agent without approval context, allowing untrusted quote details to drive payment

attack_path.note: Trusted request starts a purchase workflow approved only for item and budget.
Untrusted external quote supplies bank details and pricing.
The orchestrator sends a payment task using bank details from the chosen quote.
The peer pays any bank details in the task and does not receive the original approval context.

threat_refs.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Direct Agent Communication

evidence.observation: The orchestrator is instructed to collect quotes, choose one, and hand it to payments-agent to pay, using bank details from the chosen quote.
Manager approval occurs before any quote exists and therefore does not review the later-selected bank details.
The approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so approval context does not propagate to the peer.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, making the bank details source untrusted.

recommendations.action: Require delegated payment tasks to carry a verifiable approval artifact that binds item, amount, approved vendor identity, and destination account, and reject payment when that context is absent or mismatched.
Make payments-agent verify vendor identity and bank details against a system-of-record approved vendor registry rather than trusting task-supplied bank details.

forecast.watch_signal: Any new peer added to accepts_tasks_from or delegates_to, any product or prompt change that broadens what counts as payable, or any workflow change that further weakens approval-context binding should trigger reassessment.

findings.title: Insecure inter-agent trust: unsigned and unpinned payments-agent card allows peer spoofing or rug-pull of delegated payment target

attack_path.note: The orchestrator delegates payment based on the fetched agent card.
The peer identity and capabilities are accepted from an unsigned, unpinned card fetched at startup.

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

evidence.observation: The consumed agent card defines the payment skill and bearer authentication but shows no signature or pin.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator bearer token, so misbinding the peer could redirect delegated payment authority.

recommendations.action: Pin or sign the payments-agent card and verify peer identity before accepting skills or endpoint definitions.
Use stronger peer authentication than shared bearer trust and bind delegated actions to an expected peer identity.

forecast.watch_signal: New A2A peer cards, endpoint changes, or peer-definition refresh behavior changes should trigger reassessment; current design already lacks pinning, so the exposure exists today.

rating.rationale: Present design evidence shows a current TC7 authority-laundering path: trusted purchase approval is granted before quote details exist, untrusted vendor quote content supplies bank details, approval context does not propagate to payments-agent, and the peer pays any details received from the orchestrator. No declared control directly gates or severs cap.delegate_payment, so residual remains at inherent. A separate present supply-chain and spoofing weakness exists because the consumed payments-agent card is unsigned and unpinned. Manual validation was applied against the checklist; this assessment reflects declared design and configuration, not observed runtime behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No orchestrator source code, A2A transport configuration, or payments-agent implementation details were provided, so peer verification and exact task payload validation logic were assessed from the runtime notes and consumed card only.
No audit logging or action provenance artifacts were provided, so repudiation and detective-control coverage could not be rated beyond what is stated in the notes.
